problems.source_says: The outcome counts words in a final essay. Codebook section 6 defines category_count as counts of ideas, categories, or unique ideas coded by hand or clustering; a total word count does not satisfy that definition. The elaboration construct is supported, but this measure label is not; the supplied measure vocabulary has no explicit word-count code.
problems.quote: Length is the total essay words (𝑀± 𝑆𝐷).
problems.locator: PDF p. 15, Table 2 caption; p. 8, section 3.5.3; p. 14, section 4.2.3. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure, category_count row (line 97).

problems.source_says: This outcome analyzes PCA component scores and their condition means, measuring semantic location. Codebook section 6 defines embedding_similarity as distances between text or image embeddings. A PCA coordinate is not an embedding-distance score, so the embedding_similarity label is unsupported for this outcome even though the underlying inputs are embeddings; the other construct is appropriate.
problems.quote: To examine semantic location, embeddings from participant and AI-only essays (498 essays) were 𝐿2-normalized, pooled, and analyzed using joint PCA without condition labels.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, section 3.5.3, Semantic Content and Dispersion, PCA paragraph; p. 12, Figure 2; p. 14, section 4.2.1. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure, embedding_similarity row (line 95).

problems.source_says: The plotted measure is each content word's frequency per 1,000 essay words, averaged across essays. It computes neither overlap between texts nor type-token ratio, ROUGE, BLEU, or distinct-n, the measures covered by lexical_overlap in codebook section 6. Thus the frequency-profile description and other construct are supported, but the lexical_overlap measure label is not.
problems.quote: Each token’s count was divided by the essay’s total word count and multiplied by 1,000 before averaging across essays.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, section 3.5.3, Lexical Frequency and Source Reuse; p. 28, Appendix C, Figure 7 caption. creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Measure, lexical_overlap row (line 96).

confirmed.statement: All 12 retained outcomes are computed from the submitted Task 1 essays, rather than participants' self-reports. Semantic dispersion across writers directly satisfies criterion 3.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, section 3.5.3; pp. 12-15, Figure 2 and Tables 1-2; p. 28, Figure 7. Self-report measures are separately defined on p. 10, section 3.5.4.

confirmed.statement: AI was available during Task 1 in all three assisted conditions, including Teach-me before or without a Tell-me unlock; Human-Only had no assistant. All recorded outcomes concern immediate assisted-task output, so S1-O1 is across_people and the non-diversity outcomes are with_ai.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Introduction; p. 6, section 3.1, Condition Definitions; p. 7, sections 3.3-3.4; p. 11, section 4.1.1; Appendix D, pp. 26-29. Codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 correctly uses diversity, embedding_similarity, and set: dispersion is the mean squared distance of complete final-essay embeddings to the condition centroid. The four human condition sets exclude the separate AI-only reference.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, section 3.5.3, AI-Only Reference Corpus and equations (1)-(2); p. 13, Table 1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1: all arm counts, dispersion estimates, bootstrap limits, and printed homogenization indices match Table 1. confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, section 3.2; p. 8, sections 3.5.1 and 3.5.3; pp. 14-15, section 4.2.3 and Table 2.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because semantic dispersion is computed across participants' final essays. Three ancillary measure labels do not fit the codebook definitions (S1-O2, S1-O7, S1-O8); the recorded numerical results match the PDF, and no qualifying creative-output outcome was omitted.
